lessons.title: Close-up: brow, arm and lower edge

zoom.label: Her forehead, between the parted hair and the eyes

c1.text: Level one: her clothes date her. Now zoom to her forehead.

zoom.label: Her forehead, between the parted hair and the eyes

sources.title: The National Art Center, Tokyo, 'Masterpieces of the Renaissance from the Musée du Louvre' (2026), Fashion Characteristics
National Gallery, London, 'Italian, Milanese: Bona of Savoy (?)', collection page

c1a.text: Her hair is parted and drawn back.

correction.tempting: It runs between the two sides of her hair.
correction.truth: It is a thin band with a single jewel, worn across the forehead.
correction.evidence: National Gallery, London; National Art Center, Tokyo.

c1b.text: Too even to be a crack.

correction.tempting: Old paint does crack, as her skin shows.
correction.truth: It is a band worn across the forehead, with a jewel in the middle.
correction.evidence: National Gallery, London; National Art Center, Tokyo.

c1c.text: Yes. A thin band with a single jewel crosses her forehead, a north Italian court fashion of the 1490s.

c1m.text: A thin band with one jewel: 1490s court fashion.

zoom.label: Her upper arm on our right, where sleeve meets dress

c2.text: Level one: her sleeves are part of the fashion. Now zoom to the top of the sleeve on our right.

zoom.label: Her upper arm on our right, where sleeve meets dress

c2q.text: What holds her sleeve to the dress?

sources.title: The National Art Center, Tokyo, 'Masterpieces of the Renaissance from the Musée du Louvre' (2026), Fashion Characteristics
National Gallery, London, 'Italian, Milanese: Bona of Savoy (?)', collection page

c2a.text: Yes. The sleeve is a separate piece, tied to the dress with ribbons, with white linen puffing through the gap.

c2b.text: No buttons: the ties are cloth.

correction.tempting: Something round seems to fasten it.
correction.truth: The sleeve is tied to the dress with ribbons, the fashion of the 1490s.
correction.evidence: National Art Center, Tokyo; National Gallery, London.

c2c.text: The sleeve is a separate piece.

correction.truth: Sleeves were tied on with ribbons; you can see the gap and the ties.
correction.evidence: National Art Center, Tokyo; National Gallery, London.

c2m.text: Ribboned sleeves, tied on at the shoulder.

zoom.label: The bottom band of the painting, below her waist

c3.text: Level one: she is seen to the waist. Now zoom to the bottom of the picture.

zoom.label: The bottom band of the painting, below her waist

sources.title: National Gallery, London, 'Leonardo da Vinci: Painter at the Court of Milan', exhibition guide (2011), cat. 19
The Barber Institute of Fine Arts, Birmingham, Ingres, 'La belle Ferronnière' (drawing, about 1802-6)

c3a.text: No table: it is a stone ledge.

correction.tempting: It is flat and wide, like a table.
correction.truth: It is a parapet, a stone ledge across the front of the picture.
correction.evidence: National Gallery, London (2011); the Barber Institute.

c3b.text: Yes. A stone ledge, or parapet, runs across the front of the picture, between her and us.

c3c.text: It is painted, inside the picture.

correction.tempting: It runs right along the edge.
correction.truth: The ledge is painted as part of the picture: a parapet in front of her.
correction.evidence: National Gallery, London (2011); the Barber Institute.

c3m.text: A ledge between her world and ours.

extends.concept: From the list of her clothes (level) to the band itself: thin, with one jewel in the middle

c1q.what_you_learn: A thin band with a jewel crosses her forehead, a 1490s north Italian fashion.

regionSources.title: The National Art Center, Tokyo, 'Masterpieces of the Renaissance from the Musée du Louvre' (2026), Fashion Characteristics
regionSources.quote: the narrow decorative hairband worn across the forehead | the squared necklines and the sleeves connected to the bodice by ribbons
regionSources.supports: A narrow band across the forehead; sleeves tied to the bodice with ribbons. (Co-organised with the Louvre: counted with the Louvre.)

regionSources.title: National Gallery, London, 'Italian, Milanese: Bona of Savoy (?)', collection page
regionSources.quote: A delicate band around her forehead secures an embroidered cap on the back of her head. | as were the ribboned sleeves slashed down the back. They are worn by Beatrice d’Este in the Pala Sforzesca (Pinacoteca di Brera, Milan) and by the lady in Leonardo da Vinci’s La bell
regionSources.supports: The forehead band and ribboned sleeves of 1490s north Italian courts, worn by the lady in this painting.
